subject: FinPulse: Post-demo reliability & fallback next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@finpulse.com>, Marcello Velez <marcello@finpulse.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: FinPulse — quick recap from today’s reliability session

Hi Alicia / Marcello —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Wanted to capture the highlights so we’re aligned and to propose next steps. I’ve kept this focused on the reliability / graceful-degradation items we discussed.

Key pain points you shared
- Recent multi-region incident (Oct 2026) where latency spiked 2–3x for 25 minutes and some requests returned 503s under peak.
- Tight SLO on response P95 <= 350ms for production payment flows; current average sits ~280ms but tail is the issue.
- Regulatory constraint: customer data must remain in us-east-1 for PII; but you are open to model fallbacks running in other regions for non-PII traffic.

Current stack (as we understood it)
- Frontend: microservices in GCP us-east1, auth via Okta.
- Inference: vendor-hosted LLM endpoints (proprietary), autoscale inconsistencies during traffic surges.
- Monitoring: Datadog for metrics, but limited custom telemetry for model responses and token-level cost.

Success criteria you called out
- Predictable P95 under 350ms for payment-critical routes 99.9% of the time (target SLA).
- Fallback behavior that maintains functionality (short-form summaries) when the main model route degrades, with clear degradation ladder.
- Audit trail for routing decisions and region fallbacks for compliance.

Short-term recommendations (from our side)
- Run a 2-week pilot using Redwood’s routing + KV prefix caching to measure effective tail latency reduction and cost delta.
- Configure a fallback model variant (quantized L2) in a secondary region for non-PII traffic.
- Instrument token-level tracing and route-level tracing to capture degradation events into Datadog / Console.

Proposed next steps
1) You to share the Oct incident summary (timestamps, short root-cause notes) — Marcello?
2) We’ll produce a one-page MAP (mutual action plan) and an initial config proposal by Tue 11/10.
3) Technical sync with Marcello + Karthik to review network/region constraints — target Wed 11/11 (30 min).

Please correct anything I missed. If this looks right I’ll create the MAP and drop it in your Drive folder.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 17:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinPulse — quick recap from today’s reliability session

Thanks Rachel — this is a great summary and captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from our side:

- The Oct incident lasted ~22 minutes; source was an autoscaler misconfiguration in our current vendor that caused a delayed warm-up of new pods. We will attach the incident PDF.
- The 350ms P95 target is for the external-facing payment-confirmation endpoint only; internal admin flows can tolerate up to 700ms.
- For compliance, we need a clear statement that PII will never leave us-east-1; fallback models must operate on anonymized payloads or be regionally housed.

I’ve attached the incident summary (fp_prod_incident_summary.pdf). Marcello, can you add any technical artifacts we should share?

Also — yes on the MAP and the Wed 11/11 tech sync. 10am PT works for me.

Alicia Ramos
Head of Product Ops, FinPulse
alicia@finpulse.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcello Velez <marcello@finpulse.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinPulse — quick recap from today’s reliability session

Alicia / team — quick technical notes from my side ahead of the sync:

- Fallback strategy: Recommend a 3-tier degradation ladder:
  1) Primary: full-fidelity model in us-east-1 (PII stays local).
  2) Secondary: quantized L2 variant in us-west-2 for anonymized or token-filtered traffic (low-cost, low-latency fallback).
  3) Tertiary: edge-fast single-turn transformer (small model) in the same region as the client for critical confirmations only.

- Routing controls: Redwood can tag requests by route and customer consent flag. We can apply policy to keep PII pinned and only send sanitized payloads to secondary regions.

- Observability: suggest adding a synthetic test that simulates a 50% CPU throttle to measure warm-up time and KV cache hit-rate. That will reproduce the autoscaler-warmup symptom you saw.

- Question for Marcello: do you have any egress limits or firewall policies that block traffic to us-west-2? If so, we’ll detail a plan to proxy sanitized payloads through a us-east NAT.

I’ll prepare a short config worksheet (redwood_map_proposal.xlsx) and attach it to the MAP.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: FinPulse — quick recap from today’s reliability session

Great — thanks all. I’ve created the MAP and uploaded it to the Drive link below along with Karthik’s config worksheet. High-level MAP items:

- Pilot scope: us-east-1 payment-confirmation routes (sanitized) + secondary fallback in us-west-2 for non-PII.
- Timeline: pilot start 11/15, 2-week measurement window, checkpoint 11/22.
- Success metrics: P95 <= 350ms for payment-confirmation, tail error rate < 0.1% during peak, KV cache hit-rate > 60%.
- Deliverables: Redwood to provide config worksheet, synthetic test plan, and a draft SLA language for the pilot.
- Next meetings: Tech sync Wed 11/11 10am PT; MAP review Fri 11/13 9am PT.

Action items (owner)
- Marcello: upload any firewall/egress constraints + incident logs (ASAP)
- Alicia: confirm pilot start date and approval path (Legal/Procurement)
- Karthik: drop redwood_map_proposal.xlsx and short test plan in Drive by Tue 11/10
- Rachel: prepare draft pilot SLA and ship MAP to HubSpot deal record

If anything needs to shift, flag it here. Otherwise I’ll mark the HubSpot deal and push calendar invites for the two meetings.

Thanks —
Rachel
